tools.name: about_portaur
tools.description: Returns facts about Portaur LLC, the company behind portaur.com: who it is, its mission, its founder, how to reach it, and the public pages that say more. Read only. The facts are the ones Portaur publishes on its own site. It never returns prices, client names or anything private.

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: Lists the services Portaur offers, each with its name, a plain language summary and a fuller description, exactly as portaur.com states them. Read only. It never returns prices; pricing_approach explains how pricing works.

tools.name: contact_options
tools.description: Explains the ways to reach a person at Portaur and what each needs: a written message, a request for a phone call back, or an email. It also explains the confirmation email that follows a request. Read only. Call it before send_message or request_callback to learn what to ask the person for.

tools.name: pricing_approach
tools.description: Explains how Portaur prices its work. Read only. It returns no figures: Portaur never quotes a price through an assistant, and every project is scoped with a person.

tools.name: ask_portaur
tools.description: Asks Portaur's own assistant one question about Portaur and returns its answer, written from the same facts as the website. Read only: the question is answered once and not kept. Use it for a question the other read tools do not answer. It answers only about Portaur, never gives prices, and has a da

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Leaves a written message for a person at Portaur on behalf of the person you are helping. Needs their name, their email address and the message; a subject is optional. Use it only when the person asked you to contact Portaur. It stores the message in Portaur's inbox and sends one email to the addres

tools.name: request_callback
tools.description: Asks a person at Portaur to telephone the person you are helping. Needs their name, email address, phone number and the reason for the call; a preferred time window is optional. Use it only when the person asked to be called. It stores the request in Portaur's inbox and sends one email to the addres

tools.name: request_status
tools.description: Says how a request made with send_message or request_callback is doing, given the handle that tool returned: waiting for the person to confirm their email, confirmed and the owner has been told, or not found. Read only. It never returns the message or the address.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: contact_options, request_status · Private data: about_portaur, contact_options, send_message · Public sink: contact_options, send_message, request_callback, request_status.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: contact_options, request_status · Private data: about_portaur, contact_options, send_message · Public sink: contact_options, send_message, request_callback, request_status

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
